title: Restart sensor and preemptive restarts option no longer works with new transmitter SN 81xxxx
body: I received a new transmitter and now with the preemptive session restart set I keep getting errors. "Native Sensor is now Stopped: Sensor Failed Start" then " Native sensor is now marked FAILED: Sensor Failed Start" then "Session Start Failed: Invalid". It has been working on the last two transmitters that started with SN 80xxxx, but on the new one stating with SN 81xxxx is when i started getting these errors. Seems the only way to restart the sensor was to start it using the dexcom receiver and then i get the "Warming up" message on both xdrip and dexcom and have to wait the two hour warm up.

I am not seeing what you posted about firmware versions. You should Google restarting Dexcom sensors to make sure you do the protocol correctly. In essence you can use the combination of the official Dexcom app (though XDrip might also work, but I don't have a receiver and haven't had much luck getting two XDrip instances to pick up the transmitter properly) and the Dexcom receiver prior to the expiration of your sensor. As long as nobody will turn on the microwave for two hours you can just store the receiver in the microwave and trick the Dexcom app into thinking the sensor is new. As far as restarting XDrip manually, you can re-enter the calibration code and just tell the XDrip algorithm the approximate time you really inserted the sensor. Given my experience, I would advise you enter a fingerstick upon restarting and at least once a day afterwards because the sensor will get out of calibration and start reading over 50 points low. Finally, there should be a search box in the settings menu so you should be able to type in "preemptive restarts" and uncheck the appropriate box. The problem without the time travel is the restart reads 20 points high.

Interesting thing happened today. I put in a new G6 transmitter on September 20th. It quit getting a signal twice and they sent me a new one. However, after both events, within an hour after the customer support calls, I began getting a signal again and called and cancelled the replacement transmitter. The transmitter lost signal again yesterday. Contacted Dexcom customer support again and they scheduled a replacement transmitter. An hour or so after contacting customer service the signal returned. I contacted customer support this morning to cancel the replacement transmitter and the rep was very apologetic and said they were sorry I had lost the signal and they'd put my account on monitoring to make certain it didn't happen again. I got the impression it was something on there end that had cut the signal. (Even the Dexcom receiver would not pick up the signal.) Anyone else have similar experiences?  Another problem I have noticed is xdrip stops working and I've have to uninstall and reinstall the app and set it to  work with my SW3. Two things happened both times and I am not certain which is causing the problem. The one was the problem mentioned above. The second was a system update on my Note 9. Don't know if the combination of the two are related.

I just restarted a new transmitter successfully. I was having the same issues everyone else has had but I don't use a Dexcom receiver and use a Tandem X2 with the CGM function. I stopped the sensor in xdrip, restarted it in xdrip using code 0000, let it warm up for about 20 minutes, then stopped it again and restarted it again with the right code. I did receive a sensor failed error and invalid error once during the warmup but dismissed these errors and the warmup continued and successfully completed. I started the sensor process on the Tandem shortly after starting it on xdrip and skipped entering the code as advised since I had already started it on my mobile device. I would like to close this issue.
Please respond if you have any questions or concerns about this.

We currently can only hard reset, and perform preemptive restarts on, G6 if the firmware version is 1.6.5.25.  This includes all 80XXXX and some 81XXXX transmitters.  

Only G6 transmitters with serial numbers starting with 80 and 81 transmit raw values.  Therefore, we can only use the non-native mode on those.

Restarting any G6 transmitter whose serial number does not start with 80 or 81 requires the temporary removal of the transmitter. 

This is neither a bug, any longer, nor a feasible feature request.  Therefore, I am closing it.  
We can always reopen it if needed.  
If we find a way to change any of these limitations, we will update the documentation.
